item.title: specwizard: A Public Python Framework for Creating Synthetic Absorption Spectra from Hydrodynamical Simulations
item.description: arXiv:2610.19862v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present specwizard, a publicly available modular Python package for generating synthetic absorption spectra from hydrodynamical simulations. The code combines atomic data from the National Institute of Standards and Technology database with ionisation fractions computed using the cloudy spectral synthesis code for multiple ionising backgrounds, enabling consistent modelling of bound--bound and bound--free absorption for resonant transitions of all ions. specwizard employs a column-density--conserving projection scheme, includes natural line broadening for the Lyman series, and offers optional treatments of instrumental resolution and noise for direct comparison with high-resolution quasar spectra. As example applications of the code, we shoot sightlines through the eagle cosmological simulation to generate a z = 3.2 synthetic quasar spectrum containing H i Lyman-series transitions, including damping wings and Lyman-limit absorption. Additionally, we compute metal-absorption lines probing the circumgalactic medium of simulated galaxies, and investigate the correlated absorption of H i and Si iii. We demonstrate that specwizard applied to outputs from eagle accurately reproduces key observational diagnostics of the Lyman-alpha forest, including the redshift evolution of the mean transmission, the transmission PDF and the transmission power spectrum. We take advantage of the fact that the eagle simulation also reproduces the measured evolution of the temperature-density relation to infer the evolution of the amplitude of the ionizing background, finding excellent agreement with recent theoretical models and measurements.

item.title: Black Hole Binary Mergers in Galactic Nuclei: Combined Effects of Secular Dynamics and Stellar Flybys
item.description: arXiv:2610.19879v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Galactic nuclei, with the central supermassive black holes (SMBHs) and surrounding dense star clusters, serve as natural laboratories for studying gravitational dynamics in extreme gravitational environments. In this work, we model the long term evolution of black hole binaries (BHBs) in these environments by incorporating the tidal influence of the central SMBH, the potential of the nuclear star cluster, SMBH induced relativistic precession, and stochastic perturbations from stellar flybys. Our numerical simulations show that the long term evolution of BHBs is predominantly governed by the SMBH-driven ZLK mechanism. However, once stellar flybys are included, they can modify both the binary angular momentum and energy. The cumulative effect of repeated flyby encounters substantially reshapes the long term dynamical evolution, eventually leading systems toward either merger or disruption. Based on a population synthesis study, we find that this combined secular and non-secular channel produces a merger rate of approximately $\mathcal{R}\simeq16\mathrm{Gpc^{-3}yr^{-1}}$, which is significantly higher than the rates predicted by dynamical channels that neglect stellar flybys. Furthermore, we predict that a non-negligible fraction of merging systems would retain detectable eccentricities at low frequencies around 5 Hz, thus providing a distinctive observational signature for next generation ground based GW detectors. Our results demonstrate that the stochastic perturbations from the surrounding environment are essential for modeling BHB evolution in galactic nuclei, and that this channel may contribute a major fraction of observed mergers.

item.title: Nova shells in 3D: I. A catalog of integral field spectroscopic observations
item.description: arXiv:2610.19989v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Classical novae eject material during thermonuclear eruptions on accreting white dwarfs, forming expanding shells whose structures and kinematics provide insights into the eruption mechanism and binary interaction. However, their intrinsic three-dimensional (3D) structures remain poorly constrained. We present the first 3D catalog of nova shells based on integral field spectroscopy, enabling us to investigate their structures beyond projection effects. We compiled observations of 19 nova shells obtained with MUSE at the VLT, complemented by new MEGARA observations at the GTC and WEAVE observations at the WHT. We constructed 3D visualizations of selected emission lines to explore the diversity of shell morphologies and kinematics. The shells reveal a wide variety of structures, including ellipsoidal or spherical shells, rings, bipolar features, and clumpy or irregular components, many of which are not apparent in 2D projections. Approximately 60% of the sample exhibits predominantly ellipsoidal or spherical shapes, while about 30% shows ring-like or bipolar structures. Several objects display strong line-dependent morphological differences, with [O III] or [N II] tracing distinct kinematic components from those seen in H${\alpha}$. Compared with imaging studies, integral field spectroscopy reveals a larger fraction of bipolar or toroidal shells. The differences between emission lines highlight the diverse excitation mechanisms and physical conditions within the ejecta. Finally, comparing expansion velocities in the plane of the sky and along the line of sight suggests low intrinsic aspect ratios, consistent with estimates from projected shell shapes.

item.title: A Parsec-Scale Transient High-Frequency-Peaked Radio Source in the Very Large Array Sky Survey Brightening and Fading over a Decadal Timescale
item.description: arXiv:2610.20495v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A subset of active galactic nuclei (AGN) manifests as compact radio sources with peaked radio spectra, commonly referred to as peaked-spectrum (PS) sources. Generally, PS sources are interpreted as young radio jets, but the early evolution of the jet is rarely observed and not fully understood. Here, we present VT J182357-234511 (VT J1823-2345), a radio transient in the Very Large Array Sky Survey (VLASS) that resembles a PS source. Notable properties of VT J1823-2345 include: (i) brightening by a factor of 3 between 1996 and 2021 at 1.4 GHz, (ii) peaked spectra with high frequency peaks at $\nu_{\mathrm{p,obs}}\gtrsim6\,\mathrm{GHz}$, (iii) a peaked 3 GHz light curve that has been fading since 2023, (iv) a resolved Gaussian (major-axis) size of 0.4 mas in 2024, and (v) a linear polarization fraction $p_{\mathrm{L}}\simeq0.73\%$ at 8.8 GHz with an extreme Faraday rotation measure $\mathrm{RM_{\mathrm{obs}}} \sim +12,000\,\mathrm{rad}\,\mathrm{m}^{-2}$. On the sky, VT J1823-2345 coincides with a supernova remnant and an F-type star, but no background galaxy is seen. Based on the multi-wavelength properties, we disfavor Galactic transients, explosive extragalactic transients, and blazar variability as plausible explanations. We argue that VT J1823-2345 is consistent with a "short-lived" parsec-scale PS source with a decades-old jet that does not grow into a large-scale radio galaxy. From comparing the full VLASS light curves, we speculate that VT J1823-2345 is similar to many VLASS nuclear transients reported in the literature, which may represent an emerging class of transient radio jets, perhaps related to episodic AGN activity or jetted tidal disruption events.

item.title: Can bosenovae deplete the galactic dark matter?
item.description: arXiv:2610.20507v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: No: neither through the bosenovae of gravitational atoms formed around stars and compact objects, nor through those of boson stars formed in the galactic dark-matter halo. We assume that all the dark matter consists of ultralight bosons with attractive self-interactions, which can be captured in the gravitational potential of astrophysical objects or condense into self-gravitating configurations. When these systems collapse in a bosenova, part of their mass is turned into relativistic radiation that escapes the galaxy. We bound the mass that a single object can eject and sum it over realistic models of the Milky Way and of other types of galaxies. For gravitational atoms, with realistic stellar populations and stellar evolution, the stars of the Milky Way deplete at most $\epsilon^{\rm GA}_\star\simeq3\times10^{-9}$ of its halo, and the pump is equally negligible in other galaxies. The central black hole, Sgr A$^*$, could reach $\epsilon^{\rm GA}\sim10^{-3}$, but only for a boson mass disfavoured by ultrafaint dwarf galaxies and beyond the validity of the perturbative treatment, where only a geometric bound on the dark matter flux is available. For boson stars feeding on the rest of the halo, these would radiate at most $\sim3\times10^{-5}$ of the Milky-Way halo and $0.1\%$ of a DF2-like one.

item.title: The stellar-to-halo mass relation of central galaxies across three orders of halo mass
item.description: arXiv:2602.10193v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The stellar content of galaxies is tightly connected to the mass and growth of their host dark matter halos. Observational constraints on this relation remain limited, particularly for low-mass groups, leaving uncertainties in how galaxies assemble their stars across halo mass scales. Accurately measuring the brightest central galaxy (BCG) stellar-to-halo mass relation (SHMR) over a wide mass range is therefore crucial for understanding galaxy formation and the role of feedback processes. Here we present the SHMR spanning $M_{\rm halo} \sim 10^{12}$-$10^{15}\,M_\odot$, using halo masses derived from eROSITA eRASS1 X-ray data and BCG stellar masses based on SDSS photometry. By stacking X-ray spectra of optically selected groups, we recover robust average halo gas temperatures for each bin, which are then converted to halo masses via the $M$-$T_X$ relation. We find that the SHMR peaks near $M_{\rm halo} \sim 10^{12}\,M_\odot$, with a declining stellar fraction at higher masses. This trend reflects a combination of processes that reduce the efficiency of stellar mass growth in massive halos, such as AGN feedback, reduced cooling efficiency, and the increasing dominance of ex-situ assembly, while halos continue to grow through mergers and accretion. Our measurements are consistent over the full mass range with previous observational studies, including weak lensing, X-ray analyses of individual clusters, and kinematical and dynamical methods. Comparisons with hydrodynamical simulations show good agreement at low masses but reveal significant discrepancies in the normalization at cluster scales, highlighting the sensitivity of BCG stellar growth to feedback prescriptions and halo assembly history. These results provide the first X-ray-based observational SHMR covering three orders of magnitude in halo mass, establish a robust benchmark for testing galaxy formation models.

item.title: The DESIRED strong-line calibrations: I. New empirical metallicity relations for the local and high-redshift universe
item.description: arXiv:2604.16273v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present the most comprehensive set of empirical optical strong-line metallicity calibrations to date, based on the DEep Spectra of Ionised REgions Database (DESIRED), the largest compilation of HII regions and galaxies with direct electron-temperature determinations. We construct a high-quality calibration sample of 2392 spectra: 1029 extragalactic HII regions, 1296 local star-forming galaxies, and 67 high-redshift ($z > 2$) galaxies, drawn from 201 independent literature references, spanning $12+\log({\rm O/H}) \in [6.79, 9.07]$. Physical conditions and chemical abundances are derived homogeneously using up-to-date atomic data. We derive 27 strong-line calibrations covering oxygen-, nitrogen-, sulphur-, argon-, and neon-based line ratios, including 4 previously uncalibrated diagnostics, with reported validity ranges and intrinsic dispersions (typically $\sim0.15-0.35$~dex). For the first time in a systematic calibration framework, all relations are presented for both the homogeneous temperature case ($t^2 = 0$) and a scenario including temperature inhomogeneities ($t^2 > 0$), thereby reconciling abundances from recombination lines (RLs) and collisionally excited lines (CELs) and directly tackling the abundance discrepancy problem. A comparison with previous calibrations shows that the DESIRED relations span the broadest validity intervals while remaining anchored to the empirical data. Comparisons with $z>2$ galaxies show that several DESIRED calibrations remain consistent with independent high-redshift relations within their intrinsic scatter, whereas others display systematic offsets associated with elevated N/O or harder ionising conditions. Thus, DESIRED calibrations can provide reliable metallicity estimates at high redshift for a subset of diagnostics, while highlighting the need to account for diagnostic-specific redshift evolution.

item.title: Astrophysical Parameters of 5056 Open Star Clusters from Bayesian Nested Sampling with PARSEC Isochrones
item.description: arXiv:2605.23802v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a homogeneous catalogue of ages, metallicities, distances, and reddenings for 5056 open clusters in the Unified Cluster Catalogue (UCC), derived uniformly from Gaia Data Release 3 (DR3) colour-magnitude diagrams via Bayesian nested sampling with PARSEC isochrones. Unlike previous large-scale catalogues, metallicity is fitted as a free parameter for every cluster rather than fixed or adopted from the literature: where available, Gaia XP spectrophotometric metallicities inform the fit (1201 clusters), while the remaining clusters are constrained by broad priors from Gaia parallaxes and the Schlegel-Finkbeiner-Davis dust map. No cluster is anchored to an external open-cluster parameter catalogue, and no per-cluster manual intervention is applied. A fit-quality metric, $\eta_{\rm fit}$, identifies 3807 clusters (75 per cent) with reliable colour-magnitude solutions, spanning ages of 0.004-5.9 Gyr and distances out to 17 kpc. We validate the resulting parameters against six literature catalogues and, more critically, against independent high-resolution spectroscopic metallicities from OCCAM DR19: for 132 clusters in common we find a median absolute deviation of only 0.054 dex ($-0.021 \pm 0.132$ dex mean offset), comparable to the intrinsic systematic uncertainty of isochrone-based metallicities. As a direct consequence of this fidelity, the radial metallicity gradient recovered from our XP-informed clusters ($-0.064$ dex kpc$^{-1}$) steepens towards the spectroscopically calibrated value ($-0.079$ dex kpc$^{-1}$) for the highest-quality subset - demonstrating that a purely photometric pipeline, built without reference to spectroscopy, recovers a physically meaningful abundance scale. The full catalogue and posterior chains are publicly released.

item.title: WaveDM.jl: An Adaptable Simulation Framework for Dynamics of Baryonic and Wave Dark Matter on Galaxy Scales
item.description: arXiv:2606.25026v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present WaveDM$.$jl, an open-source Julia package for high-performance simulations of wave dark matter dynamics on galaxy scales, with a design philosophy centered on extensibility and adaptability. The code solves the time-dependent Schr\"odinger--Poisson equation (SPE) using a pseudo-spectral Fourier method. The spectral solver is tightly integrated with N-body gravitational force solvers, enabling simultaneous evolution of wave dark matter and baryonic components in galaxy-scale simulations. WaveDM$.$jl unifies shared-memory, distributed-memory, and GPU execution within a multi-level parallelization framework, enabling the same computational workflow to scale from single-node to multi-node computing environments without requiring major code changes. To further facilitate user-friendly galaxy-scale simulations, the package provides a dedicated toolbox that integrates flexible initial condition generators, trajectory lookback, tidal force calculations, and real-time visualization. Beyond astrophysical applications, the code's modular architecture and general nonlinear Schrodinger framework enable cross-disciplinary studies such as nonlinear optics and cold-atom physics. The code is open source and available on https://github$.$com/JuliaAstroSim/WaveDM$.$jl.

item.title: Continuum Variability in AGN: Evidence for Systematically Suppressed Fluctuations in the BAL Population
item.description: arXiv:2608.18287v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We aim to compare the flux variability of Broad Absorption Line quasars (BAL) to non-BAL quasars, controlling for black hole parameters to inform models concerning the generation of the BAL phenomenon. Using SDSS DR16 and ZTF $g$- and $r$-band light curves, we select quasars with $1.57 \leq z \leq 2.00$ and $18.5 \leq rmag \leq 19.8$. This redshift range ensures that the $g$-band covers the C IV emission line (and trough in BALs) while the $r$-band probes continuum variability, and allows black hole mass (MBH) estimates via Mg II. We quantify variability using excess variance and damped random walk (DRW) parameters ($\sigma_{\mathrm{DRW}}$, $\tau_{\mathrm{DRW}}$). We also compared the DRW metrics in bins of MBH and Eddington ratio (REdd) to isolate the influence of the BAL phenomenon in objects with the same physical properties. Excess variance and $\sigma_{\mathrm{DRW}}$ are consistently smaller for BALs, confirming lower long-term variability, while the $g$-band exhibits higher variability than the $r$-band across both populations. These differences persist in fixed bins of MBH and REdd, indicating that the suppressed variability in BALs is not simply driven by differences in these properties between BAL and non-BAL samples. These results show that BAL quasars are systematically less variable than non-BAL quasars in both bands, confirming that this suppression is an intrinsic feature of the continuum rather than an effect of emission or absorption line contamination. The samples could be made to agree if BAL MBH values were systematically overestimated by a factor $\gtrsim 4$, implying a significantly higher REdd. Alternatively, the lower variability in BALs can be related to their lower X-ray luminosities, or to significant nuclear obscuration, if the inner part of the accretion disc were more obscured in BALs and more variable than the rest of the disc.

item.title: The Study of Detailed Morphology of Milky Way Dwarf Galaxies: Draco and Bo\"otes I
item.description: arXiv:2609.16476v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a photometric study of the outer stellar structures of the Milky Way dwarf spheroidal galaxies (dSphs) Draco and Bo\"otes I, using deep wide-field imaging data. The old main-sequence stars are used to trace their spatial distributions beyond their tidal radii. We derive global structural parameters and radial profiles of number density, ellipticity, and position angle from their stellar distributions. Draco and Bo\"otes I show contrasting features. Draco shows no prominent extended stellar distribution, although weak elongations are detected toward the eastern and northwestern directions. Its stellar distribution remains relatively compact compared with its estimated Jacobi tidal radius ($r_J=57.2^{+13.5}_{-11.1}$ arcmin), suggesting that the stellar component is tightly bound by its gravitational potential. In contrast, the radial number-density profiles of Bo\"otes I along several directions show excess from the best-fit exponential profile outside of around $r\sim20$ arcmin, near the estimated Jacobi radius ($r_J=21.6^{+9.3}_{-7.6}$ arcmin). In addition, the ellipticity of Draco decreases with radius, whereas that of Bo\"otes I increases toward larger radii. Bo"otes I also exhibits a prominent S-shaped stellar structure extending approximately along its orbital direction. Together, the radial density excess, increasing ellipticity, and S-shaped morphology suggest that the outer stellar structure of Bo\"otes I may trace tidal tails produced by interactions with the Milky Way. The contrasting morphologies of Draco and Bo\"otes I further suggest that the response of dwarf galaxies to the Milky Way tidal field may depend not only on their orbital histories, but also on the internal structure of their dark-matter halos.

item.title: Rotational excitation of SiC$_6$ by collisions with helium: cross sections, rate coefficients and non-LTE modeling
item.description: arXiv:2610.06525v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Rotational transitions of SiC$_6$ in the $j=26$--$40$ range have been detected in IRC+10216, yet collisional rate coefficients for SiC$_6$ with He or H$_2$ were previously unavailable. This paper reports rate coefficients for rotational excitation of SiC$_6$ induced by collisions with He, calculated using a two-dimensional potential energy surface (PES) constructed at the RCCSD(T)-F12 level under the rigid-rotor approximation. The close-coupling (CC) method was employed for low rotational energy levels, while the coupled-states (CS) approximation was used for higher rotational levels. Systematic convergence tests were conducted, and the resulting CC and CS scattering cross sections were compared. The rate coefficients obtained via the CS method cover rotational levels up to $j=40$ and temperatures of 3--100\,K. Although the CC and CS rate coefficients differ by up to a factor of $\sim 2$ for some transitions, particularly those influenced by weak coupling and resonances, the two methods yield nearly identical excitation and brightness temperatures for the high-$j$ transitions (e.g., $19\rightarrow18$) examined, and the CS-based line fluxes agree with the CC-based results to within 6.5\% for $n(\mathrm{H_2}) \ge 10^{3}$\,cm$^{-3}$; this demonstrates that the CS approximation is reliable for the non-LTE modelling of high-$j$ SiC$_6$ transitions considered here, for which fully converged CC calculations are computationally impractical. Using the calculated SiC$_6$--He rate coefficients and reduced-mass scaling to estimate the corresponding SiC$_6$--H$_2$ rates, we further investigate the excitation of the observed high-$j$ transitions. Under typical low-density conditions in IRC+10216 ($n(\mathrm{H_2}) \approx 10^4$\,cm$^{-3}$), the $j=40\to39$ transition is subthermally excited, highlighting the importance of non-LTE effects when interpreting the emission of high-$j$ SiC$_6$ transitions.

item.title: Evidence of galaxy cluster rotation and intrahalo gas motions in the cosmic microwave background
item.description: arXiv:2512.10951v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We report the first robust evidence for the rotational kinematic Sunyaev-Zel'dovich (rkSZ) effect: the dipolar signal produced by the Thomson scattering of cosmic microwave background (CMB) photons off intracluster gas in dynamically active systems (including rotations and mergers). By combining CMB intensity and polarization measurements from the \emph{Planck} satellite with spectroscopic member-galaxy redshifts from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey in a sample of 25 X-ray cross-matched, low-redshift ($0.02< z< 0.09)$, massive ($10^{13.9}\lesssim M_{\rm 500c}/M_\odot \lesssim 10^{14.6}$) galaxy clusters, we detect a dipolar rkSZ signature aligned with the estimated angular momentum of each cluster, ruling out a chance fluctuation at 99.98\% confidence (3.6$\sigma$). The significance of this measurement is enhanced by several new methodological improvements for isolating the rkSZ signal from primary CMB fluctuations and noise. The amplitude and shape of the signal are qualitatively consistent with predictions from state-of-the-art hydrodynamical simulations. These results establish a new tool with which to probe the dynamical state of galaxy clusters using CMB data.

item.title: Identifying heating processes in simulations with an entropy-based scheme: A single jet episode in a galaxy cluster
item.description: arXiv:2603.26882v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Understanding heating processes in galaxy clusters is essential for predicting the regulation of radiative cooling and star formation, and for clarifying the mechanisms underlying active galactic nucleus (AGN) feedback in cool-core clusters. We investigate the processes through which AGN jets deposit heat into the intracluster medium (ICM) by tracking passive entropy scalars in magneto-hydrodynamic (MHD) simulations. This enables us to systematically disentangle the contributions from different heating channels. We successfully validate this method with several idealized tests, including turbulent heating, heating by anisotropic Braginskii viscosity, dissipative and adiabatic heating by shocks using in-situ shock-detection methods, and cosmic ray (CR) heating through the excitations and damping of Alfv\'en waves. Using this methodology, we simulate single-epoch outbursts of high-power jets with varying densities in a cluster environment. Light jets produce wider bubbles, displacing a larger fraction of the gas in the cluster's core, whereas comparatively denser jets propagate more efficiently to larger distances without significantly disturbing the central region. During early evolution, shock heating of the ICM prevails irrespective of jet density. At later times, light jets primarily heat the ICM through turbulently induced heating (which includes dissipation of vortices emerging from a turbulent cascade and mixing gas of different temperatures) and compressible dissipation of sound waves and very weak shocks, while denser jets continue to dissipate most of their energy via shocks. Particularly, turbulently induced heating by solenoidal-shear motions prevails inside the cocoon, whereas shocks and acoustic compressions dominate outside. In light jets, the forward shock weakens rapidly, whereas dense jets can sustain strong bow shocks to large distances.

item.title: Scaling Up: A Global Optical/X-ray Correlation For Reprocessing Across Black Hole Masses
item.description: arXiv:2610.17248v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This study extends the optical/X-ray correlation from black hole low-mass X-ray binaries (XRBs) to active galactic nuclei (AGN), bridging scales from stellar-mass to supermassive black holes (SMBHs). In XRBs, optical emission predominantly originates from the thermal reprocessing of high-energy photons on the surface of the geometrically thin, optically thick accretion disk. The reprocessed optical luminosity follows a power-law relation of the form $L_{V} \propto L_{X}^{\beta} a$, with $\beta \sim 0.5$, where $L_X$ is the X-ray luminosity and the orbital separation $a$ serves as a proxy for the disk size. To test the universality of this relationship across all mass scales, we analyzed quasi-simultaneous X-ray and optical flux data from a sample of XRBs and AGN that have estimates of the radius of the optically emitting disk. To bridge the structural differences between these populations, we utilized the characteristic optical/X-ray time lag derived from reverberation mapping as a physical proxy for the reprocessing radius. Our analysis reveals a tight, global correlation across all black hole masses, described by $\log L_V = 0.48\log L_X + 0.96\log a_R + 6.5$ with a scatter of $\sim 0.20$ dex, where $a_R$ is the reprocessing radius derived from the lag. Incorporating a geometric correction for the disk inclination angle ($\cos i$) slightly reduces this scatter to $0.18$ dex. These results suggest that X-ray reprocessing is scale-invariant across accretion disks, from stellar-mass black holes to SMBHs. This scaling relation provides new constraints for models of X-ray emission regions in accreting black holes.
